review.headline: A chaotic Petrov Modern Attack where an early gift made up for several of your own slips

sections.text: White's 4.Nc3?? was an early blunder and you found the right reply, 4...dxc3!, taking a knight. You were at +3.3 and the pawn on c3 stayed a thorn in White's side for several moves.
You then let it slip. 6...Nd4?? gave away the advantage (from +5.0 to +0.6); the engine wanted 6...cxb2. After 7.Nxd4? you found 7...cxb2!, which brought the pawn to b2 and kept you up.

8...b1=Q?? was a blunder, though: 8...bxa1=B was stronger, and 9.Qxb1 followed. Then 9...c6?? was another slip (-4.2), and 10.Bxf6 Qxf6 evened things out again. Both sides kept missing strong moves, and the game stayed messy until the end.
The end came after 13...Qxa1 14.Qxb7 Bxb7 15.Bxb7 Qxf1+. You were far ahead in material and White resigned.

review.turning_point: 4...dxc3! punished 4.Nc3 and gave you a large early edge that you kept even through the later errors.
review.focus: Your 6...Nd4 gave back a large edge; 6...cxb2 was there. When you are winning, prefer the move that keeps your pawn and tempo over the one that offers trades.

review.headline: A wild tactical win where both sides missed strong moves, ending in 19.Bd6#

sections.text: You took the e5 pawn early with 3.Nxe5 and played 4.Nf3. Black's 4...Bg4 and 5...Nc6 were both mistakes and you were at +2.1 after 6.h3. You played 5.Be2 and 6.h3 to challenge the bishop.

Then you gave a lot back. 7.e5?? went for a pawn push when 7.hxg4 was best, and Black missed 7...Bxf3, playing 7...Bc5 instead. After 8.exf6 and 9.fxg7 Kxg7 you were up material again, but 10.Nd4?? allowed a discovered attack and 11.Qxe2?? left a piece to be won.

Black returned the favour with 12...Qg5?? and you answered 13.d3, which opened the c1 bishop onto the queen on g5. 13.Qxg5+ was best, but it was enough: 13...Kf6 missed the threat and 14.Bxg5+ won the queen.
The finish was clean. 15.O-O, 16.Re1+, 17.Bf4+ and 18.d4+ drove the king up the board, and 19.Bd6# ended it.

review.turning_point: 13...Kf6 missed the threat created by 13.d3, and 14.Bxg5+ won the queen.
review.focus: 7.e5, 10.Nd4 and 11.Qxe2 each let the opponent back in. In a good position, take the simple capture first: 7.hxg4 and 11.Nxe2 were the engine's choices.

review.headline: A King's Knight game with wild swings, where you recovered from 4.Nxe5 and won on time

sections.text: Black played 2...h5? and 3...f6??, two weak moves that gave you a +3.0 edge. The right move in reply to 3...f6 was 4.Nh4, but you went for 4.Nxe5?? and 4...fxe5 5.Bxh5+, which dropped to +0.6.
After 5...Ke7 6.d4 Nf6 7.dxe5, Black blundered with 7...Rxh5?? and you were at +5.2. The right move was 7...Nxh5, which would have kept things much closer.
But then 8.Bg5?? gave it away, as 8.exf6+ gxf6 9.Qxh5 was the strong plan. Black missed 8...Rxg5 and played 8...b5??, and you found 9.Qxh5!, which took the rook on h5 at once.
After 10.exf6+ gxf6 11.Qh7+ Ke8 12.Qg6+ Ke7 13.Bxf6+ Ke6 14.Bxd8+ you had taken the queen, and Black lost on time.

review.turning_point: 8...b5?? missed 8...Rxg5, and 9.Qxh5! won the rook right away. From there the extra pieces made the win easy.
review.focus: You nearly gave away the game twice, with 4.Nxe5 and 8.Bg5. Before a capture, check whether a quieter move such as 4.Nh4 or 8.exf6+ keeps everything defended.
